pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING FOR FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.9: Reading for Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading for Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can reading fluently enhance our understanding of a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read simple texts fluently in Chinese

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING FOR FLUENCY
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading for Fluency helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING FOR FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read simple texts fluently in Chinese

What this means
In this part you learn to read simple texts fluently in Chinese. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read simple texts fluently in Chinese.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read simple texts fluently in Chinese. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading for Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read simple texts fluently in Chinese)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading for Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read simple texts fluently in Chinese.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading for Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading for Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading for Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can reading fluently enhance our understanding of a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading for Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read simple texts fluently in Chinese.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
